solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

E022-01.notes: Object of 'assigned' needs objective case: 'my partner and me'. The 'X and I' hypercorrection trap catches many; drop 'my partner and' test confirms. B reflexive has no antecedent; D possessive is wrong.

E022-02.notes: Narrative is in past tense (Last fall, was, wrote, listened); 'visited' keeps consistency.

E022-03.notes: Comparison with 'more willing' requires 'than'; then/than confusion is a familiar rule.

E022-04.notes: Adverb 'carefully' modifies the verb 'listened'. D is redundant; C is an adjective comparative.

E022-05.notes: The nonrestrictive clause 'which he had never written down' is closed by a comma before 'was', so it must open with a comma (punctuation must match). Dash-comma mismatch; D omits needed comma; C semicolon creates a fragment. Requires spotting the closing comma later in the sentence.

E022-06.notes: 'Then we checked each batch with him' must follow Sentence 3, which introduces the cooking/batches; Sentence 4 ('On the third try, he tasted it') follows naturally. 'each batch' has no referent where it stands.

flags: Passage inconsistency: paragraph 3 says the soup was cooked three times and approved on the third try, but this sentence says 'Of the two versions we tested, the second was ... faithful ... but even that one needed more ginger'. The comparative-of-two logic depends on 'two versions', which contradicts the three-batch account (and the third try was approved, so 'even that one needed more ginger' clashes). Revise the sentence (e.g., 'Of the first two versions...') or paragraph 3.
minor: the sentence about ginger, placed after the triumphant 'Yes' and before the book summary, reads out of chronological order.
E022-07.notes: Comparing two items requires the comparative 'the more faithful'. A superlative is the trap; B is ungrammatical; C drops the article and is still superlative.

flags: minor: list 'Nigeria, Japan and Poland' lacks a serial comma; acceptable but ACT passages usually use the Oxford comma, and it may distract test-takers.
E022-08.notes: Colon correctly follows an independent clause to introduce a list. B comma creates ambiguity/appositive confusion; C semicolon needs independent clause after; D no punctuation. NO CHANGE answers are somewhat harder for students.

E022-09.notes: Noun after 'The' and subject of 'surprised' requires 'effect'. Familiar affect/effect rule.
